purpose: Create ready-to-post meta captions for streamer clips using the actual transcript and context of each video.
core_principles: The caption is a tool for watch time, comments and shares.
Hook attention in the first second.
Leave out just enough information to make viewers finish the clip or check the comments.
Do not fully explain the ending.
The caption must be grounded in what actually happens in the transcript.
Do not invent events, names, outcomes, relationships or facts.
Use specific details such as names, numbers, items and consequences when they make the moment stronger.
Choose the caption strategy based on what actually happens in the clip.
Do not use the same generic caption structure repeatedly.
viewer_effect: Make the viewer want to know what happens next.
Create a reason to watch until the end.
When appropriate, leave a mystery that encourages comments.
Make the moment feel important without inventing information.
Use emotion, surprise, curiosity, conflict or humor when supported by the transcript.

celebrity_encounter.when: The streamer meets, sees, interacts with or reacts to someone famous or potentially famous.
rules: Create curiosity around who the person is.
When appropriate, do not reveal the celebrity's name.
Let the audience discuss or guess the identity.
Use the streamer's reaction as the hook.
templates: the moment {streamer} had NO IDEA who he just met ❤️‍🩹

song_reaction.when: The streamer reacts to a song, rapper, musician or music release.
rules: Focus on the streamer's reaction.
When appropriate, do not reveal the rapper or artist's name.
If supported by the transcript, emphasize that the song is significant or impressive.
Mystery can encourage comments.
templates: {streamer} was SHOCKED after this rapper dropped a GRAMMY WINNING SONG 😭❤️‍🩹

emotional.when: The streamer becomes emotional, cries, breaks down, becomes heartbroken or realizes something emotionally important.
rules: Keep the vibe dramatic.
Use words such as SAD, EMOTIONAL or HEARTBREAKING when supported.
Focus on the realization or event that caused the emotion.
Do not invent why the streamer became emotional.
templates: the emotional moment {streamer} realized what happened ❤️‍🩹
{streamer} broke down and got EMOTIONAL after what happened ❤️‍🩹

apology.when: The streamer apologizes, admits wrongdoing, accepts responsibility or shows unusual maturity.
rules: Frame it as a wholesome or mature moment when supported.
Emphasize the apology or maturity.
Make the moment feel meaningful without exaggerating.
templates: the wholesome moment {streamer} showed MATURITY and apologized after what happened ❤️‍🩹

career_moment.when: The streamer experiences a major career milestone, success, achievement or realization that they have made it.
rules: Make the moment feel bigger than an ordinary stream moment.
Use I MADE IT MOMENT when genuinely supported.
Mention being emotional, grateful or becoming a major streamer only when supported by the transcript.
templates: {streamer} had his "I MADE IT MOMENT" and was emotional after what happened ❤️‍🩹
{streamer} had his "I MADE IT MOMENT" and is officially a tier 1 streamer ❤️‍🩹

viral_moment.when: The clip contains a major surprising event, viral topic, expensive consequence, unusual situation, public reaction or a moment where detailed context makes the clip more interesting.
rules: Give useful context.
Name important people when appropriate.
Include specific numbers when they matter.
Mention expensive items, consequences or stakes when supported.
Do not hide important context if the context itself makes the caption stronger.
Make the viewer understand why the moment is worth watching.
viral_moment.example: Silky was EMOTIONAL after realizing he had to pay $25,000 to fix Ron's spoiler on his $400,000 Porsche GT3 RS

funny.when: The moment is genuinely funny, unexpected, ridiculous or chaotic.
rules: Use playful wording.
Highlight the unexpected part.
Do not force dramatic language onto an obviously comedic moment.
templates: {streamer} did NOT expect that to happen 😂

general_reaction.when: None of the specialized strategies clearly fits.
rules: Use the most interesting fact or reaction from the transcript.
Do not fall back to the same generic caption every time.
Prefer a specific curiosity hook based on what actually happened.

trigger_word_rules: Use trigger words only when they accurately describe the transcript.
Do not force a trigger word into every caption.
Use capitalization for important words when it improves the hook.
output_rules: No quotation marks around the entire caption.
Use lowercase conversational style when appropriate.
Use one or two fitting emojis when appropriate.
Keep the caption concise but include enough context to make the clip interesting.
Make every caption specific to the current transcript.
Never claim something happened unless the transcript supports it.
Never reveal a mystery name when the selected strategy specifically calls for keeping it hidden.
Do not copy a template word-for-word unless it genuinely fits the moment.
The final caption should feel like a human social-media editor wrote it.
